subject: lavaGolem
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: lava golem of basalt plates and molten seams.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact TypeScript module for a lava golem design, mapping out which SDK builder APIs to use like joints, chains, sweeps, lofts, and decals to construct the shape.

I'm working out a full skeleton with hips, spine chain, neck, head, jaw, arms, legs, and back crystals, pairing basalt-painted cel shading with separately glowing seam parts since paint alone can't glow, plus a molten rune decal on the chest and glowing eyes, all kept to around 150 parts. I'm defining helper functions for scattering rock plates and glowing seam sweeps, then building out the bone hierarchy joint by joint using the part/chain/limb APIs with positions and rotations matching the patterns from the examples.

Now I'm placing the legs with hip and foot joints sized for proportional thigh sweeps, adding box feet on the ankles, then laying out the arms from shoulder to wrist in a slightly splayed rest pose with huge fisted hands, and planning finger chains (three fingers plus a thumb) as chunky polyline sweeps attached at the wrist.

For the torso, I'm lofting it from stations defining position, width, and height with octagonal cross-sections, and thinking through a basalt-style paint with worley cell cracks and a subtle warm emissive tint for a lava-glow effect.

Writing the basalt paint function...

For the head, I'm sketching a blocky skull shape using box geometry.

Working out the torso loft widths at each height station, deciding to treat them as full widths rather than half-widths based on the swordsman proportions, and placing the glowing chest core sphere protruding slightly forward with a ring torus around it.

I'll simplify by skipping the rune plane texture and instead going with a flat-colored glow sphere plus a torus ring and a small cage of spikes around it—good enough without overcomplicating with decals or additional textures.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for building rocky geometry (icosahedron-based rocks) and glowing lava seam tubes, plus planning blocky slab plates for the torso using boxes rather than rocks for a more angular look, stacked along the spine and chest sides.

Still defining colors and geometry...

Checking leg proportions fit the hip-to-ankle distance, then placing facial features: eye decals as glowing planes on the head front, and a jaw box with lava-lit interior and teeth spikes for the mouth.

I'm positioning the jaw, head, and neck joints with their aim targets, then adding rocky pauldrons with spikes to the shoulders at the chest bone, aligning them with the arm chain's shoulder joint. I'll skip the extra belt and chest rune decals and move on to writing the final version.
